post.description:
Two shapes. Send exactly one of `location_id` and `calendar_id`.

- `location_id` (from `locations_list`), with `offering_id`, `team_member_id` and
  `service_address` as the location needs. A staffed location books this way. Leave out
  `team_member_id` to book the first team member who is free. Find times with
  `appointments_availability` first.
- `calendar_id` (from `calendars_list`) books a location that is not staffed on its Google calendar.

With either shape, the contact’s name, phone and email become the attendee, so reminders reach
them. The booking is made in the name of the user who created the API key.
Retry with the same `idempotency_key` to get the first booking back rather than a second one.
At a staffed location a member’s credential books and checks only its own times, and changes only its own appointments. Anything else answers 403 `insufficient_role`. A manager’s credential with the appointments power books, checks and changes anyone’s appointments at its own locations.

A refused `location_id` booking answers 409 with `error` set to one of these codes and a `message`:

- `offering_required`: the location sells services. Choose one. The body carries `booking_options`.
- `offering_not_offered_here`: the service is not offered here, or nobody here does it.
- `team_member_not_eligible`: the team member does not work here, does not do this service, or does not cover the address.
- `no_team_member_available`: nobody who can do it is free then.
- `slot_taken`: the time is booked.
- `outside_hours`: the time is outside booking hours, or outside the team member’s schedule.
- `duration_mismatch`: the end time does not match the service’s `duration_minutes`.
- `address_out_of_area`: no territory of this location covers the postal code.
- `location_changed`: the location changed while booking. Check availability again.

A `calendar_id` slot that is not available is a 409 with no code.
The same `idempotency_key` with other details is a 409 too, with no code.

info.title: Iris Public API
info.description:
The public, versioned API of Iris. Authenticate with an API key:
`Authorization: Bearer iris_sk_…`. An owner or admin mints organization keys under
Organization → API keys, and any member mints personal keys under My agent access. Keys carry
scopes; a key without a route’s scope gets a 403 with `{ "error": "insufficient_scope" }`.

Agent clients that cannot hold a key (Claude Desktop, claude.ai, ChatGPT) use OAuth 2.1 with
PKCE instead. They discover the authorization server from `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`,
and send the access token the same way. Its scopes are the scopes above.

An OAuth token acts for the person who granted it, and a personal key for its owner. That
person’s current role and locations cap it. An owner or admin can turn a person’s agent access
off, alone or by role: their personal keys and OAuth tokens then get the 401 until it is back on.
Each operation’s `x-member-access` says what a MEMBER’s credential may do: `open` (call it),
`scoped` (call it, limited to the member’s locations) or `deny` (403 with
`{ "error": "insufficient_role" }`). An OWNER, an ADMIN and an organization key reach the
whole organization. `me_get` shows the person, role and locations behind the credential.

Every path is versioned. `v1` only ever grows: a breaking change ships as `v2`, and the
old version keeps serving with `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers until it is retired.

servers.description: REST base URL. The MCP server (Streamable HTTP) is https://api.iris.dotfun.co/api/v1/mcp, with every operation below as a tool named by its operationId.

apiKey.description: An organization API key: the opaque `iris_sk_…` string shown once at creation. An OAuth access token from the Iris authorization server is accepted here too.

name.description: Event name whose enrollments should be cancelled for this contact.

reason.description: Why the journey ended. Defaults to `goal_met`.

name.description: Event name. Matched as free text against the `event_name` of every active `event` sequence in the organization.

key.description: Caller-owned idempotency key for this event. Stable for "the same logical event", so a redelivery is a no-op. Surrounding whitespace is trimmed.

supersedes.description: Events whose running enrollments this one REPLACES. Cancelled after this event claims its `key` and before it enrolls, so a redelivery with the same `key` cancels nothing and enrolls nothing. Use this for mutually exclusive states of one subject; use the top-level `cancel_events` for an unconditional exit.

email.description: Contact email address — the upsert key, matched case-insensitively

phone.description: Contact phone number. Stored in field_values; the contact itself stays email-keyed with phone_number NULL.

fields.description: Arbitrary key/value data merged into the contact's CRM field values. At most 200 keys. With assessment_abandoned, user_message_count must be a numeric nonnegative safe integer when present. Cohort routing uses this request's count: started requires a positive count, never_started requires zero, and missing counts match only unfiltered triggers.

cancel_events.description: Sequence events to CANCEL for this contact, unconditionally. Processed before `events`, and idempotent because a second call cancels nothing. Use it for a goal exit, such as ending a win-back nurture once the contact converts.

events.description: Sequence events to FIRE for this contact, after the cancellations. Each event in turn claims its `key`, cancels the enrollments named in its `supersedes`, then enrolls. An event with no subscribing sequence leaves its key unspent, so a later retry still enrolls.
